principles.text: He rarely manages stops (rarely trails or raises to breakeven); the hard stop is a protective/precautionary measure for sudden gaps or black swans, while actual selling is discretionary, taking names off before they reach the stop.
After a crazy rally and a change-of-character distribution candle, either sit out doing nothing or look for the short side; don't keep buying.
Bullish medium-term but patient short-term: wait for volatility to tighten and the indices to digest selling (e.g. reclaim the 60-min 9 EMA) before opening new longs.
Study weekends focusing heavily on past trades, especially the losses; a cluster of ~20 losing trades late in a move was an early warning that justified sizing down before the market broke.
Reflect on exits even for winners; selling ARM fully then failing to hold/re-buy cost a 100% move — exits are the weakest part of his game.

Shorting is much harder than going long and is best only when the general market is clearly weak (e.g. Qs below 50 EMA); shorting a leader rallying into declining EMAs while the index is still in an uptrend is low-probability.
Cover shorts into weakness; expect a strong bounce after a big down day, especially in volatile leveraged ETFs, so cover near the lows rather than risk being shaken out.
Relative strength of IWM / individual stocks vs the indices during a pullback (e.g. names holding the weekly EMAs) is a green flag for the market's medium-term health.
